title: Two White Doves
summary: Elia and her family are going to bring a gift to the Mishkan. Everyone brings big gifts, and all Elia has is two little doves in a basket. A warm story about how a gift is measured by the heart, not by its size.
pages:
A bright morning in the camp.
Today all the families are going to the Mishkan to bring a gift to God.

Elia walks with Abba and Ima.
In her hands is a little straw basket, and inside it are two white doves.
"Coo, coo," say the doves.

Suddenly a tall man walks past her.
He is leading a big bull, a huge one, with horns and a bell around its neck.
"Boom, boom," go the bull's feet.

Behind him comes a family with a plump white sheep.
And after them, a boy with a hopping goat.

Elia looks at her basket.
Her doves are so small.
"Ima," she whispers, "maybe our gift is too small?"

Ima bends down to her.
"We give what we have," she says, "and we give with all our heart.
And God loves gifts that come from the heart."

Elia thinks.
She remembers how every morning she gave the doves seeds,
how she stroked them, and how she sang them a song.

They arrive at the Mishkan.
The priest smiles at Elia, the very same smile he smiled at the man with the big bull.

"What a beautiful gift," says the priest.
"The Torah says that even two doves, or a little flour, are a complete gift."

Elia holds out the basket with both hands.
Her heart grows wide, as big as a bull, and maybe even bigger.

On the way home, Elia skips along.
"Ima," she says, "my gift wasn't small.
It was exactly the size of my heart."

And what about you?
A little drawing, a hug, or helping at home can be a big gift too,
when you give it with all your heart.
